first_impression.reaction: Googled 'paros wedding venues' because Paros is on our list as the quieter option to Mykonos, and I'm comparing three planners. The intro sorts the island by area and gives guest count, ceremony type and rooms as the criteria. No 'paradise'. Went to the FAQ first, then the table, then the capacity section, and only read properly the two venues that publish numbers, plus weather and legal. It keeps admitting what it doesn't know, it dates the stale venue pages and says the weather comes from Naxos. I trust it more for that. Two small things bugged me: the line that Villa Mira is 'the only' exclusive-use venue when The Secret View also gives you the whole place, and the legal section leaning on a Smartraveller line about 'some countries' without saying whether Greece is one of them.

journey.quote: The right one depends on your guest count, the ceremony you want (chapel, beach or terrace) and whether you would rather your guests sleep under the same roof.

Few Paros venues publish a wedding capacity, and the clearest figures belong to Petra Farm (a chapel for 120 and an event space for 150) and The Secret View (110 for a terrace ceremony, 120 for dinner).
journey.reaction: Opens by telling me the data is thin and then gives me the numbers that do exist. That's the right order.

journey.section: Paros wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: It is not a ranking. "Not published" means the venue does not state the detail.
journey.reaction: Six of eight capacity cells say 'Not published'. Annoying, but honest. Better than a made-up number I'd catch later.

journey.section: Paros wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: When you have a shortlist, book a Wedded Concierge consultation to test them against your dates and guest list.
journey.reaction: Booking link before I've read a single venue entry. It's conditional ('when you have a shortlist'), so it's not pushy. Minor.

journey.quote: Ask for current wedding terms, as that page dates from 2018.
journey.reaction: Telling me the source is eight years old is exactly what I'd have found myself and then held against you. Good.

journey.quote: The farm limits itself to 10 weddings a year, and its team is on site to oversee every supplier for the whole rental period.
journey.reaction: A hard number and a concrete operational detail. This one goes in the spreadsheet.

journey.section: Villa Mira Paros, above the Bay of Parikia
journey.quote: The only venue here that offers the whole property for your day.
journey.reaction: Two sections earlier you told me The Secret View gives 'full access to every area of the venue for 24 hours'. That's the whole property too, it just has no beds. Small, but it's the kind of 'only' I check, and it doesn't hold.

journey.quote: Arriving by boat at the dock is the detail guests will remember.
journey.reaction: Says who? It's the one line in the entry that's mood rather than fact. Harmless, but I noticed it.

journey.section: The Secret View at Fladakia Estate, above Golden Beach
journey.quote: House rules are published: loud music stops at 2am, out of respect for the local villages, with a quieter after-party (an acoustic band, for example) possible.
journey.reaction: A curfew, a time, and bring-your-own suppliers. These are the catches I'm looking for and they're on the page. Per-space capacities above it too.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most often with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and registry certificates.
journey.reaction: 'Some countries'. Is Greece one of them or not? The section is dated and linked, which I like, but it never actually says what Greece requires. I get that the municipality doesn't publish it, and the page says so, but this line reads like an answer when it's a generic one.

journey.section: Civil, Greek Orthodox and symbolic ceremonies
journey.quote: A church ceremony takes place in one of the island's churches or chapels.
journey.reaction: Civil is defined as a legal marriage, symbolic as not legal. The church option is left in the middle. Is a Greek Orthodox wedding legally binding on its own, and do we both have to be Orthodox? Not answered.

journey.quote: The national weather service publishes no climate figures for Paros, so the figures below come from the nearest official station, on Naxos.
journey.reaction: Real numbers by month, with the source and the limitation stated. This is the section I'd send to my dad.

journey.quote: Ask every venue on your shortlist these questions, and get the answers in writing:
journey.reaction: 'In writing' is the bit I care about. The list is the stuff that bites you later: curfew, minimum stay, set-up times.

journey.section: Shortlist your Paros venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. Still doesn't tell me whether any of these venues pay you too.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues, and does that affect which ones the Wedded Advisor recommends?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee calculated and what does it cover?
Does Greece specifically require a CNI from Australians, or is that just a general Smartraveller point?
Is a Greek Orthodox church wedding on Paros legally valid on its own, and are there conditions (e.g. both partners Orthodox)?
How many guests can Villa Mira's four villas sleep, and does it host a ceremony on site?
Is there a real Paros wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: The only venue here that offers the whole property for your day.
turn_offs_found.why: The page itself says The Secret View gives couples full access to every area for 24 hours, and the FAQ lists both together. An 'only' that the same article contradicts makes me recheck the other superlatives.

turn_offs_found.quote: Arriving by boat at the dock is the detail guests will remember.
turn_offs_found.why: It's a prediction about my guests with nothing behind it, in an entry that is otherwise all facts from the venue. Minor.

turn_offs_found.quote: When you have a shortlist, book a Wedded Concierge consultation to test them against your dates and guest list.
turn_offs_found.why: It sits straight after the table, before any venue is described. The wording is conditional and soft, so it's low severity, but the pitch still comes before the proof.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the comparison table and the Petra Farm and Secret View entries (the only two with real capacities and house rules)
My dad, the Naxos weather figures and the heat and wildfire paragraph, plus the Embassy section

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, shortlist your Paros venues with a Wedded Advisor.
cta_reaction.why: The page mostly earned it: blanks admitted, stale venue pages dated, curfew and supplier rules named, weather with a real source and a stated limitation, and a checklist that says 'in writing'. What stops me is the legal section not telling me what Greece actually requires, and I still don't know whether you take a cut from the venues. I'd check those before booking a call.

top_3_changes: Fix the Villa Mira 'only' line (must-fix, small): 'The only venue here that offers the whole property for your day' contradicts The Secret View's 24-hour full access stated in the same article and the FAQ. Reword to something like 'the only venue here where guests can sleep on a property you have to yourselves', or drop 'only'.

Tighten the legal section: the Smartraveller 'some countries' line reads like a Greece answer when it isn't. Say plainly that the page can't confirm whether Greece requires a CNI and that this is the first question for the municipality and the Embassy. Also say whether a church ceremony is a legal marriage or flag it as a question to ask, so the three paths are equally clear.

Optional polish: drop or soften 'Arriving by boat at the dock is the detail guests will remember', and consider moving the first Concierge link below the first venue section. (Commission and fee-model detail would help me most, but that is a deferred business detail, so nice-to-have.)

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and table first, cross-checked claims against each other, looked for catches, fee model, commissions
No invented brand facts; fee, commission and real-budget details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'how we know' lines

open_questions.question: Does the source pack say anything Greece-specific about the CNI or the legal status of a Greek Orthodox church wedding? If not, should the writer state the gap plainly rather than lean on Smartraveller's generic 'some countries' line?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'paros wedding venues' while comparing three planners; Paros is one option among several, hence relevance 4 rather than 5.
No prices on the page is deliberate and not penalised.
Venue descriptions attributed to the venue (e.g. 'with the deep blue of the Aegean Sea in the background') are not counted as the brand's own unsupported claims.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not flagged.
